requirement: A price catalog that memoizes loader calls in a bounded LRU cache owned by each catalog instance, normalizes SKU keys before caching, exposes hit/miss stats and capacity, supports invalidation, and lets a dropped catalog be garbage collected.
skeleton: PriceCatalog wrapping its loader in a per-instance functools.lru_cache with normalization, stats, capacity, and invalidate.
caption: A standard-library price catalog that memoizes lookups with functools.lru_cache without the usual method-cache leak. The module defines DEFAULT_MAXSIZE as 128 and a PriceCatalog class whose constructor takes a loader callable mapping a SKU string to a Decimal and a maxsize defaulting to DEFAULT_MAXSIZE. A maxsize below 1 raises ValueError with a message saying it must be at least 1. Instead of decorating the method at class level, which would key the cache on self and keep every catalog alive, the constructor wraps its private _load method in lru_cache(maxsize=maxsize) and stores the wrapper on the instance, so each catalog owns its own cache and is freed with it. price(sku) strips surrounding whitespace and upper-cases the SKU before calling the cached wrapper, so equivalent spellings share one loader call. stats() returns a tuple of cache hits and misses from cache_info, the capacity property returns the cache's maxsize, and invalidate() calls cache_clear so the next lookup reloads. The fixture asserts that AB-1 and "  ab-1 " produce one loader call with stats (1, 1), that two catalogs with different loaders return their own prices, that invalidate forces a second load, that the default capacity is 128, that maxsize 0 and -1 raise ValueError, and that a dropped catalog is collected after gc.collect.

plan.intent: Memoize catalog price lookups in a cache each catalog owns
constraints: The cache defaults to 128 entries and is created per instance, not on the class
SKUs are stripped and upper-cased before the cache lookup
stats returns hits and misses, and invalidate clears the cache
A dropped catalog must be garbage collectable

rationale.teaches: Wrapping a bound method in functools.lru_cache inside __init__ so each instance owns a bounded cache keyed on normalized arguments.
rationale.why: A cache that looks right in one call hides three bugs: equivalent keys that miss, a clear that never happens, and an unbounded or shared cache. Only calling the loader and counting its calls shows which lookups actually reached it.

ops.docstring: Cache catalog price lookups per instance so a dropped catalog frees its cache.

candidates.why_wrong: A maxsize of 0 or less is accepted, so the catalog is built with a cache that never stores anything.
The default cache is unbounded, so a long-running catalog grows without limit.
The raw SKU is used as the cache key, so a padded lower-case spelling calls the loader again.
The SKU is lower-cased instead of upper-cased, so the loader receives a key it does not know and prices come back as zero.
invalidate leaves the cache intact, so a changed price is never reloaded.
